rituals.name: THE ODDS RECEIPT
rituals.unique_game_move: Score Odds → Weigh Evidence → Follow Evidence
rituals.recognition_cue: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
rituals.immediate_need: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
rituals.match_reason: Probability overestimation · Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
rituals.goal: Fear speaks in certainty; reality keeps percentages.
rituals.steps:
1. Score Odds — Give the prediction a number from 0 to 100.
2. Check Baseline — Find one real reference point: how often has this happened in similar situations?
3. Weigh Evidence — Notice one fact that raises the odds and another that lowers them.
4. Revise Odds — Pick a new number and remember it.
5. Follow Evidence — Act from the revision, not the original alarm.
rituals.win: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Disaster stopped being the only ending.
rituals.tips:
• You do not have to solve the worst-case forecast at its loudest.
• Pause fear forecasting; give the next practical step a fair chance.
• Do not let certainty inflation turn discomfort into a command.
• Keep the next move connected to perspective.
• Choose actual probabilities while worst-case living is still only an option.

rituals.name: THE BAD VOICE ACTOR
rituals.unique_game_move: Read Wrong → Keep Words → Replay
rituals.recognition_cue: Authority often hides inside delivery.
rituals.immediate_need: Authority often hides inside delivery.
rituals.match_reason: Unexamined belief · Authority often hides inside delivery.
rituals.goal: Authority often hides inside delivery.
rituals.steps:
1. Read Wrong — Hear the thought as a tired GPS, an overdramatic sports commentator, or a hesitant intern reading the wrong memo.
2. Keep Words — Keep the words unchanged; alter only tempo, pitch, and confidence.
3. Replay — Then replay it in your natural voice as a possibility, not an order.
rituals.win: ✓ A fixed rule turned back into a context-dependent idea.
rituals.winReward: ✓ A fixed rule turned back into a context-dependent idea.
rituals.tips:
• Keep responsibility proportionate when rigid certainty gets personal.
• Protect mental flexibility; rigid certainty does not need every answer.
• Let one fresh question make the situation easier to carry.
• Let a more flexible interpretation create a little distance from rigid certainty.
• Make room for a wider view instead of feeding rigid certainty.

rituals.name: EDIT THE FONT, NOT YOURSELF
rituals.unique_game_move: Project → Move Metres → Read Version
rituals.recognition_cue: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
rituals.immediate_need: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
rituals.match_reason: Unexamined belief · A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
rituals.goal: A thought displayed differently can be held differently.
rituals.steps:
1. Project — Project the sentence on an inner screen.
2. Shrink — Shrink it to caption size.
3. Move Metres — Move it two metres away.
4. Lower Opacity — Lower opacity, swap the heavy typeface for something ordinary, and place generous blank space around it.
5. Read Version — Read the edited version once, then look at real text nearby.
rituals.win: ✓ The thought changed format, and some of its spell broke.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The thought changed format, and some of its spell broke.
rituals.tips:
• Choose one fresh question while rigid certainty is still only an option.
• Even with a fixed story, you can still choose a more flexible interpretation.
• Let perspective grow quietly beside an old label.
• Give a fixed story time to change before choosing rigid certainty.
• New evidence deserves a chance to update an old conclusion.

rituals.name: RETURN WITHOUT A TRIAL
rituals.unique_game_move: State Off → Name Value → Skip Verdict
rituals.recognition_cue: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
rituals.immediate_need: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
rituals.match_reason: Value disconnection · Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
rituals.goal: Drift needs a direction change, not a prosecution.
rituals.steps:
1. State Off — State what moved off course in plain language.
2. Delete Adjectives — Remove every adjective about your character.
3. Name Value — Name the value still available, then take the smallest move that serves it now.
4. Check After — Only after moving, decide whether the plan itself needs repair.
5. Skip Verdict — Re-enter the plan without putting yourself on trial.
rituals.win: ✓ Re-entry happened without opening a courtroom.
rituals.winReward: ✓ Re-entry happened without opening a courtroom.
rituals.tips:
• Protect purpose by refusing to rush into forced meaning.
• Let the ache of change exist while you protect connection.
• Choose gentle remembrance; relief can arrive before certainty.
• Give yourself one response that supports direction.
• Use what still matters when a meaning struggle starts feeling permanent.

rituals.name: COMPLETE THE DEFENCE IN MINIATURE
rituals.unique_game_move: Small → Stop Completion → Observe Whether
rituals.recognition_cue: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
rituals.immediate_need: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
rituals.match_reason: Impulse fusion · An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
rituals.goal: An interrupted protective move may still be waiting.
rituals.steps:
1. Small — Notice the small impulse to push, turn, step back, shield, or say no.
2. Let Unfold — In a safe space, let it unfold slowly at ten percent strength.
3. Stop Completion — Stop at the natural completion and return to neutral posture.
4. Observe Whether — Observe whether the body receives an ending.
rituals.win: ✓ The urge peaked without becoming a contract.

• Keep craving escalation from turning a craving into a bigger problem.
• Give a deliberate response more authority than impulse obedience.
• Choose more options first, then decide what the urge needs.

rituals.recognition_cue: Not every unsettled breath needs a longer exhale.

rituals.name: FOLLOW IT TO ZERO
rituals.unique_game_move: Select Naturally → Identify Instant → Let It End
rituals.recognition_cue: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.
rituals.immediate_need: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.

rituals.goal: A thought’s disappearance is usually ignored.

1. Select Naturally — Select one naturally occurring thought.
2. Stay Wording — Stay with its exact wording or image as it alters, fragments, loses relevance, or is replaced.
3. Identify Instant — Spot the first instant when no trace can be found.
4. Let It End — Do not resurrect it to verify the ending.
rituals.win: ✓ The thought ended. I did not drag it back for an encore.
rituals.winReward: ✓ The thought ended. I did not drag it back for an encore.

• Let a familiar belief be difficult without making rigid certainty necessary.
• Do not use premature closure as proof that a familiar belief is correct.
• Give choice a chance before repeating label obedience.
• Let perspective set the direction when a familiar belief feels loud.

rituals.name: NOT THIS, STILL HERE
rituals.unique_game_move: Body → Keep Perspective → Rest Unlabelled
rituals.recognition_cue: Remove identities without attacking experience.
rituals.immediate_need: Remove identities without attacking experience.
rituals.match_reason: Dissociation drift · Remove identities without attacking experience.
rituals.goal: Remove identities without attacking experience.
rituals.steps:
1. Body — Notice body, sensation, thought, emotion, and role in turn.
2. Keep Perspective — For each say, ‘Observed—therefore not the whole observer.’ Do not claim they are unreal.
3. Rest Unlabelled — After the sequence, rest with what remains unlabelled, then reconnect to name and place.

• Make room for the room around you instead of feeding story chasing.

rituals.unique_game_move: Ask Far → Park Scenario → Decide Information
rituals.recognition_cue: Not every distant scenario deserves a seat in this decision.

rituals.name: MOVE BEFORE THE MOOD
rituals.challenge: Knowing the first task but avoiding it
rituals.primary_trigger: Knowing the first task but avoiding it
rituals.unique_game_move: Action threshold: Open the door → Choose one inch → Run one minute → Stop at proof → Leave a doorway
rituals.recognition_cue: Use one small action to start before motivation arrives—without solving everything.
rituals.situation: Knowing the first task but avoiding it
rituals.immediate_need: Use one small action to start before motivation arrives—without solving everything.
rituals.match_reason: Action threshold · Use one small action to start before motivation arrives—without solving everything.
rituals.goal: Use one small action to start before motivation arrives—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Open the door — Put the needed file, tool, or item in front of you. Nothing else is required.
2. Choose one inch — Pick the smallest action you can finish quickly. Let that count.
3. Run one minute — Work only until one quiet minute has passed. Keep the next part outside.
4. Stop at proof — Pause when you can see evidence that you started. Do it once.
5. Leave a doorway — Set up the easiest next action before stepping away. Take a normal breath.
rituals.win: ✓ One small move worked—you made a visible start.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One small move worked—you made a visible start.
rituals.tips:
• For action threshold, change one visible thing at a time.
• Keep the first round shorter than your resistance.
• End while the next step is still obvious.
• Let a rough beginning count as real progress.
• Make the first move physical, not theoretical.

rituals.ritualText:
THE KEY GETS ONE VOTE

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

say the important part without stacking every issue—with one small action.

1. Choose one sentence — Write the message in one plain sentence first. Nothing else is required.
2. Keep it observable — Describe what a camera could have seen or heard. Let that count.
3. Say what you need — Name the boundary, concern, or impact directly. Keep the next part outside.
4. Make one request — Ask for one specific change or next action. Do it once.
5. Stop after the message — Do not weaken the point with a long defence. Take a normal breath.

WIN

✓ You turned the conversation into one workable message in one short round.

TIPS

• For conversation avoidance, change one visible thing at a time.
• Kindness does not require a long explanation.
• Pause after the message and allow a reply.
• Say what you will do, not what you will force.
• Remove old history that does not belong to today.

MIND BEND

One clear issue is easier to solve than five tangled ones. Choose one sentence → Say what you need → Stop after the message: That is enough for this round.

FORMULA FLOW

Choose one sentence → Keep it observable → Say what you need → Make one request → Stop after the message

SAFETY

PAUSE
Step away if the interaction is abusive, threatening, coercive, or unsafe. Use appropriate personal, workplace, legal, or professional support when needed.

rituals.name: HAND ONE-INCH SWITCHBOARD
rituals.challenge: Nobody is sure who owns the next step
rituals.primary_trigger: Nobody is sure who owns the next step
rituals.unique_game_move: Ownership blur: Name the decision → Show the evidence → Choose the owner → Set the next action → Send the short update
rituals.recognition_cue: Use one small action to give the team one shared next step—without solving everything.
rituals.situation: Nobody is sure who owns the next step
rituals.immediate_need: Use one small action to give the team one shared next step—without solving everything.
rituals.match_reason: Ownership blur · Use one small action to give the team one shared next step—without solving everything.
rituals.goal: Use one small action to give the team one shared next step—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Name the decision — State what must be decided or changed. Nothing else is required.
2. Show the evidence — Use one concrete example, date, result, or observation. Let that count.
3. Choose the owner — Name who is responsible for the next action. Keep the next part outside.
4. Set the next action — Choose one task with a clear deadline. Do it once.
5. Send the short update — Share fact, impact, owner, and next step only. Take a normal breath.
rituals.win: ✓ One small move worked—you gave the team a shared next move.
rituals.winReward: ✓ One small move worked—you gave the team a shared next move.
rituals.tips:

• Use one observable example.
• Close the loop after the action is done.
• Separate the fact from your assumption.
• Name the owner of the next action.

rituals.name: THE NARROW RECEIPT TEST
rituals.challenge: An employee keeps missing a clear expectation
rituals.primary_trigger: An employee keeps missing a clear expectation
rituals.unique_game_move: Accountability drift: Write the issue → Make the impact visible → Set the expectation → Set the next action → Send the short update
rituals.recognition_cue: make ownership and the next action clear—without solving everything.
rituals.situation: An employee keeps missing a clear expectation
rituals.immediate_need: make ownership and the next action clear—without solving everything.
rituals.match_reason: Accountability drift · make ownership and the next action clear—without solving everything.
rituals.goal: make ownership and the next action clear—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Write the issue — Describe the people issue in one neutral sentence. Give it ten seconds.
2. Make the impact visible — Explain what the issue affects and why it matters. One pass is enough.
3. Set the expectation — Define what a completed result looks like. Return if attention slips.
4. Set the next action — Choose one task with a clear deadline. Choose safety over speed.
5. Send the short update — Share fact, impact, owner, and next step only. End at the first useful shift.

• Keep impact practical rather than dramatic.
• Record the handoff in plain words.
• Set a date or check-in point.

rituals.goal: Use one small action to settle your pace and deliver the first clear point—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Set your posture — Lift the chest slightly and loosen the shoulders. Nothing else is required.
2. Rehearse the first line — Say the opening once in plain words. Let that count.

5. Finish the point — Complete the sentence before judging the result. Take a normal breath.

• Keep both feet supported while you speak.
• Finish the sentence before grading yourself.

rituals.match_reason: Last-minute self-doubt · act with enough confidence for the next move—without solving everything.
rituals.goal: act with enough confidence for the next move—without solving everything.
rituals.steps:
1. Plant your feet — Feel both feet and let the floor carry you. Give it ten seconds.
2. Practice ten seconds — Run only the beginning, not the whole performance. One pass is enough.
3. Pause before speaking — Let one quiet beat settle the pace. Return if attention slips.
4. Focus on the message — Choose clarity over trying to look confident. Choose safety over speed.
5. Finish the point — Complete the sentence before judging the result. End at the first useful shift.

A SIDE LAUNCHPAD EXIT

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

act with enough confidence for the next move—without solving everything.

1. Plant your feet — Feel both feet and let the floor carry you. Give it ten seconds.
2. Practice ten seconds — Run only the beginning, not the whole performance. One pass is enough.
3. Pause before speaking — Let one quiet beat settle the pace. Return if attention slips.
4. Focus on the message — Choose clarity over trying to look confident. Choose safety over speed.
5. Finish the point — Complete the sentence before judging the result. End at the first useful shift.

WIN

✓ You used action to create usable confidence.

TIPS

• For last-minute self-doubt, change one visible thing at a time.
• Let one imperfect word pass without restarting.
• Name one thing that worked, then move on.
• Confidence can arrive after the opening.
• Finish the sentence before grading yourself.

rituals.ritualText:
UNHOOK THE NARROW PULSE

PLAY TIME

60–90 seconds

GOAL

lower the alarm enough to stay with this minute—without solving everything.

1. Feel the floor — Press both feet down and notice the support. Stop there.
2. Slow the exhale — Breathe out a little longer than you breathe in. Keep it small.
3. Name three colours — Look around and name three colours you can see. Do not plan ahead.
4. Rate the wave — Give the panic wave a number from zero to ten. Use the easiest version.
5. Choose the safe next — Pick the least harmful action available now. Stay with this round.

WIN

✓ You stayed with the minute instead of the forecast.

TIPS

• For acute panic surge, change one visible thing at a time.
• Delay messages and decisions until the heat drops.
• Use ordinary sights and sounds as anchors.
• Treat one calmer notch as a real shift.
• Choose the least harmful next action.

MIND BEND

A body alarm can feel urgent without predicting what happens next. Feel the floor → Name three colours → Choose the safe next: That is enough for this round.

FORMULA FLOW

Feel the floor → Slow the exhale → Name three colours → Rate the wave → Choose the safe next

SAFETY

PAUSE
If symptoms may reflect a medical emergency, severe withdrawal, immediate danger, self-harm risk, violence risk, or inability to stay safe, seek urgent professional or emergency help rather than continuing self-help exercises.
